question: In an intrinsic semiconductor, explain why the number of free electrons is equal to the number of holes. How does this affect its electrical conduction?

options.A: The number of electrons exceeds holes because every broken covalent bond creates two electrons and no hole.
options.B: In intrinsic semiconductor, each thermally broken covalent bond produces one free electron and one hole simultaneously. Thus $n_e=n_h$, and both electrons and holes contribute to electrical conduction.
options.C: The number of electrons equals holes because neither carrier can move; therefore intrinsic semiconductor has no conduction.
options.D: Holes are absent in intrinsic semiconductor because electrons never leave covalent bonds.
